Subject: Mutual Action Plan: Sprint Owners, Acceptance Gates & Fallback Runbook

Hi all,

Attached is a working Mutual Action Plan (Nimbus MAP v1.2) to guide the next 8-week onboarding sprints. Key points:

- Week 1-2: Provisioning & secure connectivity (Redwood infra team / Nimbus SRE)
- Week 3-4: Model integration + QA (Redwood integrations / Nimbus Data team)
- Week 5: Acceptance testing window (owner: Nimbus PM)
- Week 6-8: Performance tuning, ramp, and go/no-go cutover

I've included an "Acceptance Criteria Checklist" and a short "Fallback Runbook" for quick reference. Please review owners and acceptance gates in column C-D of the MAP and call out any team-level blockers by EOD Wednesday.

Specific asks:
1) Marissa — confirm CS handoff date and one primary contact for weekly ops check-ins.
2) Ben — procurement / billing milestone: can we confirm when the PO is expected to clear? (See the procurement row.)
3) Jordan — are the provisioning windows below realistic for Nimbus's maintenance calendar?

Emily/Carlos — if anything in the schedule conflicts with your internal programs, mark the MAP and suggest alternate dates directly in the sheet.

Thanks,

--
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0173

Thanks Soojin — quick read-through below. High level: looks good. Couple of tactical edits and one ask from CS:

- Handoff: propose CS weekly bridge starts Tue 2029-05-28 (weekly 30m sync). Primary CS owner will be Marissa Cole (marissa.cole@redwood.ai).
- Acceptance Gate (Week 5): Add SLA smoke tests (latency < 250ms P50, throughput baseline) as mandatory criteria. See row 27.
- Ramp window: recommend moving performance tuning earlier into Week 4 to allow an extra verification cycle before cutover.

Action items I will take: update MAP with the weekly sync recurring invite, add the SLA smoke test checklist to the Acceptance PDF, and draft a short customer-facing "what success looks like" note for Nimbus stakeholders.

Ben — did procurement share a tentative PO clearance date? We need the billing milestone aligned before provisioning finalization.

Emily — quick sanity check on the Week 3 test cohort (10 prod-like requests/min, replayed). If that's too heavy, tell us preferred throughput for the first test.

Marissa

Thanks for the clear MAP — couple notes from Nimbus:
1) Week 1 provisioning window: Our SRE team has a maintenance blackout on 2029-05-29. Can we avoid that date for the first provisioning attempt?
2) Week 3 test cohort: prefer starting with 5 requests/min for the initial replay and escalate to 20 req/min in the subsequent cycle. We want to validate correctness first, not load.
3) Acceptance criteria: happy to run the SLA smoke tests but would like the acceptance doc to include an explicit pass/fail definition for tokenization disagreements (we'll add examples).

Also looping in Carlos for procurement cadence — Carlos, any update from your side that changes Ben's timeline?
